articles.title: Egypt: At least 31 dead after fuel truck overturns on highway
articles.summary: The accident occurred on the packed Ring Road in Giza near Cairo. Dozens of ambulances are responding to the crash, and Egyptian health authorities say the death toll could rise.

image.caption: Rescue workers rushed to the scene and pulled people out of burning cars Image: Mohammed Salah/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: A fuel truck overturned on a packed highway in Giza, Egypt, on Wednesday, killing 31 people and injuring 21 more, according to Egyptian authorities.
What do we know so far?
The fuel tanker crash ignited a massive blaze on Ring Road in Giza's Waraq district. The Ring Road encircles the greater Cairo metropolitan area.

Egyptian Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar said the injured were transported to nearby hospitals and added that the death toll could rise further. He said 39 ambulances are responding to the accident.

blocks.caption: Cars were seen burned out after the accidentImage: Mahmoud el-Khawas/AFP

blocks.text: A massive fire broke out after the accident, with rescue workers pulling people from their vehicles. A large crowd gathered in the densely populated Waraq neighborhood amid the rescue efforts.
An investigation has been launched into the crash, according to Egypt's public prosecutor. DNA tests are being carried out to identify badly burned victims of the blaze.
El-Sissi expresses condolences to the victims

Egyptian President Abdel-Fattah el-Sissi expressed his deepest condolences and sympathy to the victims and directed relevant authorities to provide necessary support to the families of the victims and the injured.

Italian Foreign Affairs Minister Antonio Tajani said he extended his "deepest solidarity to the victims' families," Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty "and to the Egyptian people, whom I count as friends, at this tragic time."
Car accidents are frequent in Egypt due to poor road conditions, reckless driving and lax enforcement of safety rules.

articles.title: At least 30 killed in massive fire as fuel truck crashes on Cairo highway
articles.summary: Another 19 are injured after the tanker reportedly overturns on a busy ring road in the Egyptian capital.

blocks.text: At least 30 people have been killed and 19 others injured in a large fire on a busy highway in Cairo after a fuel tanker crashed, Egypt's health ministry says.

Hospitals nearby treated patients suffering burns and smoke inhalation after the incident, which occurred on a section of a ring road in the Warraq neighbourhood, to the north of the old city centre, on Wednesday evening.
Unverified footage circulating on social media showed billowing flames and black smoke towering high into the night sky, with multiple nearby vehicles torched.
Officials have not given an account of how the fire broke out, but state-owned media reported the fuel truck had overturned, dousing nearby vehicles with petrol.
The regional public prosecutor has launched an investigation into the incident and asked that DNA samples be taken from bodies of the dead.

The tanker, which belonged to a private contractor, had been travelling along the highway when a high-voltage cable fell in front of it, prompting the driver to lose control, Al-Ahram reports, citing sources with knowledge of the investigation.
It then crossed the central reservation, overturned and caught fire, the state-owned newspaper says.

Egypt has suffered several deadly fires in recent years, with informal residential areas and often run-down infrastructure making incidents more common, the response to which is often complicated by slow emergency response times and locally improvised rescue efforts, even in the sprawling Egyptian capital.
Images from the scene show a large crowd gathered on the highway after the fire had been extinguished, as emergency services blocked off entry routes.

articles.title: Margaret Atwood, bird advocates say fight against Ontario island telecom tower is gaining steam
articles.summary: Canadian author Margaret Atwood says she has heard a lot of public support for a full impact assessment of a proposed telecom tower for Pelee Island in southwestern Ontario. Atwood and other bird…

image.caption: Celebrated Canadian author Margaret Atwood cuts the ribbon at the opening of the Atwood Gibson Bird Centre in September. Atwood is honorary chair of the Pelee Island Bird Observatory. (Pelee Island Bird Observatory)

blocks.text: Windsor

Canadian author Margaret Atwood says she has heard a lot of public support for a full impact assessment of a proposed telecom tower for Pelee Island in southwestern Ontario. Atwood and other bird advocates are seeking to stop the planned 200-metre tower from going forward.
U.S. finance company building the tower says it has conservation in mind and has already consulted
Canadian author Margaret Atwood and other bird advocates say they’ve seen a swell of public support in their quest to stop a planned 200-metre telecom tower on Pelee Island.

The Pelee Island Bird Observatory (PIBO), which counts the celebrated novelist as an honorary chair, said Wednesday that in under a week, more than 27,000 people sent letters supporting a federal impact study of the project. The non-profit expects that decision by Jan. 19.
The letter writers’ fears, PIBO says, are the same as Atwood’s — that the tower’s height, lights and guy wires will hurt birds flying Canada’s southernmost migratory route.
“We are not done,” Atwood, who was born in Ottawa and turned 87 last week, said Wednesday. “We will keep going. We will see what happens and we’ll see that Canada does the right thing.”
Pelee Island, seen in this aerial photo, is in the western basin of Lake Erie in Essex County. (Photo courtesy Ontario-Canada-Travel)
DRW, a Chicago-based financial trading firm, plans to build the tower next year.

The company said in a statement this month that it’s committed to environmental protection. It also said it went through a public consultation period as part of a process with Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada.

items: Margaret Atwood joins other bird lovers to fight against a proposed 600-foot tower on Pelee Island

blocks.text: "We are committed to voluntarily installing best-in-class bird collision mitigation technologies alongside the lighting requirements for aviation security," DRW said in a statement.

"We have welcomed the Pelee Island Bird Observatory’s feedback on those plans. We will continue that dialogue as the project progresses, with a shared goal of protecting the birds that travel through Pelee Island."

But Atwood said she and others were blindsided when they heard about the tower this fall. It was right around the time the nearby Atwood Gibson Bird Centre opened. She spent years fundraising for the project. The tower would be about two kilometres away, on 1245 Centre Dyke Rd.
Caldwell First Nation says it was also not consulted.
Tower project went to council 3 years ago
Township bylaws show the tower project first came to local council in 2023 and was formalized further in 2025.

items: New home for bird migration science on Pelee Island, honours the legacy of Margaret Atwood and Graeme Gibson

blocks.text: PIBO has sent the township a number of requests for information, said director Matthew Gibson. It also hopes to appear before council on Dec. 8.

A council of five governs the island, a tourist destination that has a year-round population of fewer than 300 people. PIBO estimates about a million birds fly over the island as they cross Lake Erie at the confluence of two flyways.
CBC Windsor is pursuing comment from Pelee Island council members. Coun. Dean Robillard said he hasn’t “been given any information with regards to the tower.”

articles.title: Final Avengers: Doomsday trailer racks up over 500 million views in 1st day
articles.summary: On Tuesday, Marvel released the final trailer for the upcoming Avengers movie, and it generated 563 million views in the first 24 hours. That makes it the most viewed Disney trailer of all time,…

image.caption: Avengers: Doomsday hits theatres on Dec. 18. It will be the first Avengers film since Avengers: Endgame in 2019. (Marvel Studios)

blocks.text: Entertainment·New

On Tuesday, Marvel released the final trailer for the upcoming Avengers movie, and it generated 563 million views in the first 24 hours. That makes it the most viewed Disney trailer of all time, beating out the previous Avengers: Doomsday teaser, which hit 503 million views in the first 24 hours.
While many fans are hyped, some have called out some of the trailer's visuals
It's safe to say there's a fair amount of hype around the upcoming release of Avengers: Doomsday.
Marvel released the final trailer for the upcoming superhero movie on Tuesday, and after just 24 hours it had already generated 563 million views.

That makes it the most viewed Disney trailer of all time, beating out the previous Avengers: Doomsday teaser, which hit 503 million views in the first 24 hours. It's also already the second most viewed movie trailer of all time, just below Spider-Man: Brand New Day, which has over 718 million views.
The film, directed by Anthony Russo and Joe Russo — who also directed Avengers: Infinity War and Avengers: Endgame — is set to hit theatres Dec. 18.

The trailer starts by showing Steve Rogers, played by Chris Evans, as he talks about fatherhood, and if he should tell his son about his past life as Captain America and an Avenger. He's then approached by Reed Richards, played by Pedro Pascal, and the rest of the Fantastic Four.
That's followed by a shot of Doctor Doom, played by Robert Downey Jr., accompanied by three mysterious masked women.

More heroes meet each other (and in some cases fight) including Canadian Simu Liu as Shang-Chi, Ian McKellen as Magneto and Chris Hemsworth as Thor. Though he doesn't appear in this trailer, Doomsday will be the final big-screen role for Patrick Stewart, who plays Charles Xavier, the leader of the X-Men.
Mixed reviews
"My family and I have booked the entire movie theatre for ourselves for the premiere of Avengers: Doomsday," posted X user @JesabelRaay. "They all couldn't stop talking about the new trailer."
But not all the hype is positive.
In the final scene, many of the heroes come together on a sort of battleground, and viewers weren't impressed.
"Avengers: Doomsday looks hideous … it visually looks awful," said @constantine_james7 in a video on Instagram.
Another Instagramer, @screened_scored, said it looked like "they took a bunch of individual characters, cut them out, and placed them against a digital background."
What is hype worth?

The last Avengers film, 2019's Avengers: Endgame, made $2.9 billion US at the box office (With a bump from the recently released slightly updated version) making it the highest-grossing movie of all time, not accounting for inflation.
But other recent films with high trailer views have done well.
While many fans are excited for the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday movie, some took to social media to complain about some of the visuals in the latest trailer. (Marvel Studios)
The hype around Spider-Man: Brand New Day translated into box office success, with the movie pulling in $2.52 billion US worldwide
Deadpool & Wolverine's 2024 Super Bowl teaser scored 365 million views if you include those who watched the trailer during the Super Bowl broadcast, and that movie took in $1.3 billion US globally.
Possible hidden secrets
Keen-eyed viewers believe they aren't exactly seeing everything in these trailers.

At the end of the recent release, many of the heroes team up for a classic "Avengers, assemble" shot that often accompanies these big team-up movies when all the heroes unite to fight against common enemy.
But some viewers have pointed out that there are some gaps where they believe characters have been digitally edited out.
While much of the cast has been announced, there are still some unknowns around who will appear in the movie, such as three characters pictured here. (Marvel Studios)
It wouldn't be the first time.

In a trailer for Spider-Man: No Way Home, Tobey Maguire and Andrew Garfield playing their versions of Spider-Man were edited out of the trailer that otherwise would've shown them swinging into action with Tom Holland's Spider-Man.
In trailers for Endgame, Thor and Bruce Banner's Smart Hulk were edited out of scenes, so it wouldn't give away their appearance.
Tickets for the Dec. 18 release of Avengers: Doomsday have been on sale since July. It will premier the same day as Dune: Part Three directed by Canadian Denis Villeneuve.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Philip Drost is a network senior writer for CBC News based in Fredericton. You can reach him at philip.drost@cbc.ca.

articles.title: Buster the hamster home safe after hitching ride in Halloween pumpkin
articles.summary: A adventurous hamster named Buster is back home in Arnprior, Ont., three weeks after hitching a ride inside a discarded Halloween pumpkin and ending up on a farm about 20 kilometres away.

image.caption: Covered in orange pumpkin juice, one family’s pet hamster, Buster, turned up inside a donated pumpkin that was left for over 21 days. (Castlegarth Farms/Facebook)

blocks.text: Ottawa·New
A adventurous hamster named Buster is back home in Arnprior, Ont., three weeks after hitching a ride inside a discarded Halloween pumpkin and ending up on a farm about 20 kilometres away.
Couple found Arnprior family's pet on their farm 3 weeks later and 20 km away
· CBC News
· Posted: Nov 25, 2026 3:39 PM EST | Last Updated: 8 minutes ago
Every November, Matthew Brearley and Tanya Sprowl collect donated pumpkins at Castlegarth Farms in White Lake, Ont., where they're used for compost.
The couple told CBC’s Ottawa Morning that they typically inspect the pumpkins for non-compostable items such as forgotten tea lights.

"We go through each pumpkin, piling it on the compost pile, and there was quite a sizable amount," Brearly said. "I was turning it over, looked down and saw what I thought was not a hamster, but [another kind of] small rodent, which does happen on farms."
But after a closer look, Brearley realized this was no typical farmyard rodent, but a domesticated hamster that's definitely not native to the Ottawa Valley.
Buster had spent an estimated 21 days inside the pumpkin, where he at least had plenty to eat.
"He was quite wet, he was covered in pumpkin guts and juice," said Sprowl. "So he was a little scraggly, but he seemed otherwise OK and didn’t have any injuries."
'That's Buster!'

Brearley scooped the hamster up and brought him into the house to be properly fed and cleaned. Figuring he was someone's missing pet, the couple took Buster's "mug shot" and posted it to a local Facebook group in an attempt to find his owners.

"He must have crawled into one of their Halloween pumpkins to have a snack and then ended up in the pile at the Nick Smith Centre bound for a dump truck that was headed to our farm for composting," the Facebook post read.
Word spread quickly.
"People followed the story all weekend looking for updates. It was kind of funny,” Brearley said.
Eventually, a family from Arnprior reached out.
"They sent us a direct message saying, 'That’s Buster!’ and they had been tearing their house apart for the last three weeks looking for their hamster," Sprowl said.
Sprowl said Buster was finally reunited with his owners after being "fluffed up" and made more presentable. Buster's family, which includes three boys, declined to comment for this story.
Brearley said it was an unexpectedly happy ending to a remarkable adventure.
"I would’ve been surprised if my hamster disappeared three weeks ago. I would’ve assumed it gone forever, but there it was, no foul and reunited with its family,” he said.
"He’s one lucky hamster that’s for sure,” the couple wrote on Facebook, thanking the online community for helping make Buster's homecoming happen.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Cassandra Bellefeuille is a journalist with CBC Ottawa. She covers municipal affairs, politics and local news. She holds a combined honours degree in journalism and political science from Carleton University.

articles.title: PQ urges other parties urged to sit in Quebec legislature — despite recent ruling ordering oath to King
articles.summary: The battle over whether Quebec legislators will have to swear an oath to the King continues, with an appeal hearing scheduled for Friday. The premier wants his opponents to join him in sitting in the…

image.caption: Parti Québécois House leader Catherine Gentilcore (left) and Quebec's minister of justice, Marie-Claude Sarrazin (right), confirmed at the National Assembly on Wednesday that their party was ready to sit as planned next Tuesday, regardless of the outcome of ongoing legal proceedings relating to legi

blocks.text: Montreal·New

The battle over whether Quebec legislators will have to swear an oath to the King continues, with an appeal hearing scheduled for Friday. The premier wants his opponents to join him in sitting in the legislative session, regardless of the outcome of the court ruling.
Superior Court ruling suspended law that made oath optional; appeal to be heard Friday

Quebec Premier Paul St-Pierre Plamondon is encouraging his opponents to join him in taking their seats at the National Assembly next Tuesday, despite a Quebec Superior Court judge’s ruling ordering legislators to swear allegiance to the King before sitting at the National Assembly.
Justice Ian Demers warned on Monday that laws passed at the National Assembly could be rendered invalid if members do not take the oath.
The government is contesting the decision. The appeal will be heard at 2 p.m. on Friday in Montreal.
"We believe that, in any case, there is absolutely nothing preventing us from sitting," said Parti Québécois (PQ) parliamentary leader Catherine Gentilcore on Wednesday.

Even though the appeal has not yet been heard, the premier has sent a letter to the leaders of the three opposition parties, urging them to commit "to begin our parliamentary work on December 1, with our oaths as they currently stand."
During the swearing-in ceremonies of each party, the MNAs made their oaths to the Quebec people. It was Bill 4, passed unanimously in Quebec in Dec. 2022, that made the oath to the Crown optional.

Demers said in his Monday ruling, though, that the Quebec government had overstepped its constitutional boundaries with this law. He wrote that "the Constitution is not an à la carte menu" from which individuals can pick and choose what to follow.

items: Quebec's legislative session in limbo as court mandates oath to the King
Could the Parti Québécois actually abolish the monarchy in Quebec?

blocks.text: All the parties have said they want the legislative session to start next Tuesday as planned. However, they've expressed varying degrees of resistance to pledging allegiance to King Charles.
Quebec Liberal Leader Charles Milliard has said he won't rule out taking the oath.
"It wouldn't be responsible to close any doors except the one that we will not be postponing the session," he said on Tuesday.
Quebec Conservative Party Leader Éric Duhaime has voiced support for protecting the parliamentary sovereignty of the National Assembly, while also showing a willingness to be flexible.
"It's not because you know you're saying those words before you're getting into the House that necessarily you become a federalist and a monarchist," Duhaime said.

items: Lieutenant-governor will skip Quebec cabinet's swearing-in at incoming premier's request

blocks.text: Meanwhile, the province's political parties have reached an agreement to change another National Assembly rule.

When the premier marks the opening of the legislative session, the new Speaker of the National Assembly will table the written speech of the lieutenant-governor, who's a representative of the monarchy.
The lieutenant-governor has traditionally delivered an opening address at the start of a new legislative session.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Patricia Kozicka is a digital journalist with CBC Montreal. She has previously worked in Toronto and Edmonton. You can reach her at patricia.kozicka@cbc.ca.

articles.title: Liberal senator Leah Blyth announces defection to One Nation
articles.summary: South Australian senator labels One Nation the ‘only party with the bold ideas needed to turn this country around’

blocks.text: Leah Blyth, federal Liberal senator for South Australia, has announced she is defecting to One Nation, becoming the party’s first upper-house member for the state.
Blyth, a member of Angus Taylor’s shadow cabinet, said she did not believe the Coalition was capable of opposing the Albanese government, which was “running the country into the ground”.
“I can no longer in good conscience tell Australians that the Liberal Party can save this country,” she said in a statement.
“Australia is a country worth fighting for … I want our children to grow up proud of their country, with the freedom and opportunity to build a better life.
“One Nation has never shied away from confronting the uncomfortable truths facing our nation. They are the only party with the bold ideas needed to turn this country around.”
Pauline Hanson welcomed the South Australian senator, and said she would “build on One Nation’s expanding support within the state”.
Hanson posted a video to social media on Wednesday night, cooking a steak in a sandwich press and asked viewers to “guess who this is for”.
It was a reference back to the same meal shared between the One Nation leader and then-Nationals MP Barnaby Joyce ahead of his defection.
On Thursday morning, Nationals leader Matt Canavan called Blyth’s defection “disappointing on a number of levels” and condemned the move as part of a broader pattern of behaviour from One Nation.
The deputy Liberal leader, Jane Hume, similarly described the move as a “disappointing decision” but said Blyth “wasn’t a big contributor to the party room”.
Speaking to Radio National, Canavan said the move took him by surprise.
after newsletter promotion
“I try and be friends with everyone … and I thought I was friends with Leah, but there was no warning from her.”
Speaking to Blyth’s reasoning that her values aligned closer to One Nation, Cavanan said the move “smacks of self-interest to me”.
“Good luck to her. Leah went to the election last year supporting net zero. She didn’t oppose the hate speech laws earlier this year, like we did - the Nationals.
“To turn around now a few months later and say, ‘my principles and policies are more aligned with One Nation’ – I mean, give me a break.”

articles.title: Nigeria detains 5 Mexicans, confiscates over $220 million of meth
articles.summary: Nigeria's anti-drug agency said Mexican experts were allegedly recruited by a Nigerian national to run a meth laboratory in the southeastern state of Enugu.

image.caption: At least 10 Mexicans are now in Nigerian custody, including five from an earlier raidImage: NDLEA/Handout/REUTERS

blocks.text: Nigeria's National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLA) said Wednesday it had arrested five Mexicans and confiscated over $220 million (around €200 million) in methamphetamine as part of a significant drug bust.
What do we know about the drug bust?
The agency said the Mexican experts were allegedly recruited by a Nigerian national to run a meth laboratory in the southeastern Nigerian state of Enugu.

"A total of 1,512 kilograms of methamphetamine, finished and in production, with an estimated value of $226.8 million was recovered from the clandestine factory," NDLA spokesperson Femi Babafemi said.

Nigeria first rejected the entry of the Mexicans into the country in August. They later entered Nigeria again in September via neighboring Benin using forged passports, with authorities then putting them under surveillance.
On November 11, the Mexicans were taken into custody at the Enugu lab after their movements were tracked by the Nigerian government. A Nigerian was also arrested in a nearby hotel.

blocks.caption: Nigerian authorities inspected the Enugu facility and seized industrial equipment along with chemicalsImage: NDLEA/Handout/REUTERS

blocks.text: The latest drug bust comes after Nigerian authorities in May also detained 10 people in a anti-meth operation in the southwest, including three Mexicans.
Why do Mexican cartels find African countries desirable for drug production?

The arrests raise concern that Mexican cartels are getting a foothold in Africa for international drug trafficking. In addition to Nigeria, South Africa is another country where Mexicans have been arrested for being involved in a meth lab.

According to Vanda Felbab-Brown, an expert at the Washington DC-based Brookings Institution, Mexican cartels such as the Sinaloa Cartel and the Cartel de Jalisco Nueva Generation (CJNG) have expanded their operations into other continents such as Africa.
How drug cartels expand their reach across West Africa

In a June testimony to the US Senate Caucus on International Narcotics Control, Felbab-Brown said the cartels find "desirable partners" for production in countries such as South Africa and Kenya due to factors such as "limited law enforcement capacities and entrenched criminal and corrupt networks."
According to the UN Office on Drugs and Crime,criminal networks often take advantage of porous borders in the West and Central Africa region to carry out activities such as illicit drug trafficking.

"Many countries in the region have vast territory and borders are located either in very remote or densely populated areas, thus making law enforcement activities particularly difficult to conduct in an efficient manner," the office said. "The porous nature of the borders in West and Central Africa is a major factor of insecurity: the borders are neither demarcated or sufficiently controlled."

blocks.text: Energy minister says geopolitical tension ‘infected’ Cop31 talks

blocks.caption: Catie McLeod

blocks.text: Catie McLeod
The energy minister, Chris Bowen, has said the failed Cop31 negotiations he presided over were more strained than previous years.

Bowen, who served as president of negotiations at the talks in Turkey, was interviewed on the ABC’s 7.30 program last night about the conference, which did not result in consensus among the countries over a proposed “cover decision”, or an overarching agreement, for the conference.
Bowen told the ABC it was not unusual that the negotiations were difficult, but:

double quotation markThe difference this year was countries were a lot harder to budge from their position and frankly I felt a lot of geopolitical tension in the room on other issues infecting the conversation and making it so much harder to negotiate. I’ve been to five Cops, seen plenty of argy-bargy, but there was a lot more rigidness to the negotiations this year. We [Australia] have always supported transition away from fossil fuels. This year I had a slightly different job. Normally we go – I go – to Cops and argue for what should be in. This year my job, running the negotiation – was to find ... the strongest outcome that I could get 195 countries from Tuvalu to Saudi Arabia to agree [on].
As Guardian Australia previously reported, the biggest sticking point was whether the agreement would mention the need for the world to transition away from fossil fuels.

blocks.caption: Tess Ikonomou

blocks.text: Tess Ikonomou
Labor and Coalition on cusp of gas deal
A federal scheme requiring Australia’s largest gas exporters to keep up to a fifth of their product for domestic use is likely to be announced, with Labor and the Coalition on the cusp of a deal.
The Albanese government and the opposition have been locked in negotiations to reach an agreement before parliament breaks for the year after Thursday.
Labor agreed to a carve-out from the policy for Western Australia, as the mining state already has its own reservation scheme.
But the Coalition has held out over a provision that will require gas companies to oversupply the market by 10%, arguing it will affect future investment.
The opposition has remained the government’s partner of choice for this policy, as the Greens demanded a 25% tax on gas exports in return for their support.
Welcome
Good morning and welcome to our live news blog. I’m Martin Farrer with the top overnight stories and then it will be Krishani Dhanji with the main action.

articles.title: Judge orders transfer of Thomas Markle to face formal charges in California
articles.summary:
Father of the Duchess of Sussex currently being held in Florida is charged with possession of child pornography

A judge in the US has ordered the transfer of Thomas Markle, the Duchess of…

blocks.text: A judge in the US has ordered the transfer of Thomas Markle, the Duchess of Sussex’s father, to California to face formal charges of possessing child sex abuse images.

The move comes after a federal grand jury on the west coast paved the way for the prosecution of Markle Sr, who is currently being held in custody in Florida. He was charged with two counts of possession of child pornography.
The transportation of Markle Sr to the charging jurisdiction was ordered by the magistrate judge Lindsay Griffin in Florida on Wednesday, according to documents seen by the Press Association.
The 82-year-old is expected to appear before a Los Angeles judge in the coming weeks, where he will hear the charges against him and is likely to be asked to enter a plea.
The grand jury filing alleges that on or about 30 October and 4 November of this year, Markle Sr “knowingly possessed 35mm film negatives that contained child pornography”.

The negatives are alleged to include images that “involved a prepubescent minor and a minor who had not yet attained the age of 12 years old”. If convicted, he faces up to 20 years in prison on each count.
Markle Sr was detained by FBI agents on 6 November after they seized a cache of material from two Los Angeles storage units that he rented for nearly two decades.

He came under investigation after he was reported to police in the Philippines and the FBI last month by his son, Thomas Markle Jr, who allegedly found illegal images in his father’s belongings in Cebu City.
Markle Jr told the Sun newspaper he had tipped off the authorities about the LA storage facilities.
The US attorney’s office for the central district of California stated: “Every defendant is presumed to be innocent until and unless proven guilty in court.”
After initially being released on conditional bail following his arrest in Florida, Markle Sr was detained just days later after removing his electronic monitoring tag.
During his interview for this, Markle Sr claimed not to understand the allegations against him and that he did not have “any child porn” and “no pictures of naked kids”.
Meghan, who moved back to the UK with the Duke of Sussex in August, has said previously she was “deeply distressed” at the accusations against her father, from whom she is estranged.

She revealed she was sent a letter via the Metropolitan Police and Royalty and Specialist Protection in 2019 which made “troubling and disturbing allegations” about her father, but she was given assurances these were being investigated.
The Met has admitted it never shared the details with other law enforcement agencies, with the police watchdog, the Independent Office for Police Conduct, now investigating the force’s conduct.

articles.title: Oregon man and dog narrowly escape being swept away by high tides as officials urge caution at beaches
articles.summary:
Record-breaking king tides have prompted west coast authorities to warn residents to stay away from beaches

The US west coast has seen record-breaking tides this week and authorities have…

blocks.text: The US west coast has seen record-breaking tides this week and authorities have urged residents to avoid beaches, but not everyone is heeding those warnings.

In Cannon Beach, Oregon, viral footage showed a man and his dog nearly getting swept away by a so-called king tide on Tuesday morning. The man had been standing on a staircase holding his leashed dog, who was walking in the sand, when the water suddenly surged, knocking him to his feet.

They ultimately escaped without injury, according to the Cannon Beach police department. Earlier that morning, police had cited the same man for driving on the shoreline. He had reportedly “indicated” to an officer he wanted to get a better look at the high tides.
Other footage captured around Cannon Beach on Tuesday morning showed a jogger narrowly avoiding a major wave, while another stood amid the wave seemingly filming.

King tides are the highest tide cycles of the year. This winter, conditions caused by the super El Niño have pushed these tides to record levels, contributing to widespread flooding, powerful waves and coastal erosion.
The Cannon Beach police department advised residents to stay off beaches and keep pets away from the water.

“King tides are an impressive natural phenomenon, but no photograph, video or closer look is worth risking your life, the life of your pet or the lives of the first responders who may be called upon to rescue you,” the police department said in a statement.

A coastal flood advisory is in effect for the region through Thursday, according to the National Weather Service, as “king tides, elevated seas, and the arrival of fresh swells likely lead to tidal overflow”.

articles.title: High levels of salmonella found in some products from nation’s biggest turkey producer
articles.summary:
Two years of inspections at four Butterball plants show rates far exceeding US averages in ground or chopped meat

Inspectors found salmonella bacteria in more than a third of ground or…

blocks.text: Inspectors found salmonella bacteria in more than a third of ground or chopped turkey samples at slaughterhouses owned by Butterball, the US’s biggest turkey company, data shows.

The US Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) food safety and inspection service (FSIS) and some states conduct regular checks for salmonella and other bacteria in commercial poultry plants. Salmonella can live in the intestines of poultry, and it can cause nausea, diarrhea and even death in humans if meat is not cooked properly and then consumed.

This story is published in partnership with investigative journalists at the publication SourceMaterial, which analyzed fiscal year 2025 and 2026 FSIS inspection data provided by animal-rights campaign group Project Slingshot. SourceMaterial verified the data and found that ground or chopped turkey contamination rates from all Butterball’s slaughterhouses were well above the industry average.

Just under 43% of ground or chopped turkey sampled over the past year at four Butterball plants contained the pathogen. No contamination was identified in Butterball’s whole birds or ready-to-eat (cooked) products.

But at its Mount Olive factory in North Carolina, the nation’s biggest turkey slaughterhouse, FSIS inspectors found salmonella in 16 of 45 ground or chopped turkey samples tested at Mount Olive, or 36%. That’s well above the USDA’s acceptable limit for salmonella contamination in individual plants, which is 13.5%. A slaughterhouse does not face any fine if it exceeds this limit nor does it have to recall products. But the USDA does require it to explain how it is addressing the issue.

The high prevalence of salmonella is concerning because the Mount Olive plant processes 285,000 birds a week and sells raw ground turkey, burgers and sausages nationwide. The company supplies the three biggest US supermarkets – Walmart, Costco and Kroger – as well as fast-food companies.

A Butterball spokesperson said in response to the contamination data: “At Butterball, food safety is critically important, and we work diligently to ensure consumers can feel confident in the products they prepare and serve to family and friends. We continue to invest in new technologies, strengthen our processes, and work with food safety experts to advance our practices and reduce pathogens, including salmonella.”

They also said the company was taking part in a pilot program with FSIS “evaluating the cause of foodborne illness” and pointed out that none of the company’s pre-cooked products contained salmonella.

Alice Johnson, senior vice-president of food safety, quality and animal care at Butterball, said the company believes FSIS should measure the quantity of salmonella in samples, not simply whether or not it is present, although experts interviewed by SourceMaterial disagreed.

“Yes, having less harmful salmonella contamination is better than having more of it,” said Sarah Sorscher, director of regulatory affairs at the Center for Science in the Public Interest. “You know what is even better still? Having no salmonella in your food. That’s sadly not where we are right now.”

At Butterball’s main rival, Jennie-O, 7% of ground and chopped turkey samples tested positive for pathogens in the last year. A spokesperson for Jennie-O said that the company’s food-safety program was “robust” and noted that its results “compare favorably to industry averages and remain well below applicable regulatory performance standards”.
Sorscher explained that ground and chopped turkey might be prone to higher contamination because “every processing step is another opportunity for the meat to become contaminated”.

Tests also found evidence of drug-resistant superbugs. Two-thirds of samples taken from birds’ intestines across all of Butterball’s slaughterhouses in the fiscal year 2026 that contained salmonella and campylobacter (another pathogen that can sicken humans) showed strains resistant to at least one antibiotic. Doctors often use antibiotics to treat severe cases of both infections.
Butterball’s Johnson pointed out that the drug-resistance tests use samples from whole birds and so do not necessarily show “contamination in finished poultry products”.
The government data covered the entire US meat industry, showing an average 12% of samples contaminated with any pathogen and 33% of pathogens resistant to drugs.
“I don’t see how we can call our food system the safest in the world when we don’t have standards to prevent people from getting sick from eating the poultry,” said Sorscher.

Thomas Gremillion, director of food policy at the Consumer Federation of America, said salmonella contamination is worsened by fast line speeds at slaughterhouses. The Trump administration has allowed poultry processors to boost line speeds to kill more animals per minute.

Faster speeds make it harder “to keep the animal viscera and what’s in the digestive tract from getting on the meat”, he said. “Beyond just being disgusting, it’s a food safety risk because that’s where the pathogenic bacteria concentrate.”

And, said Dani Replogle, an attorney at the non-profit Food & Water Watch, faster production means “more antibiotics in feed and in water” – which is at odds with Donald Trump’s promise to get chemicals out of our food. He has yet to move to reduce antibiotic use in the food supply.

Each year, about 25,500 Americans are hospitalized after being exposed to salmonella and campylobacter, leading to 435 deaths, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. In 2019, Butterball recalled almost 80,000lbs (36,000kg) of turkey products from Mount Olive after an outbreak of illness across two states likely caused by salmonella linked to the company’s products.

The number of samples detecting antibiotic-resistant bacteria were comparable at Butterball and Jennie-O. At Butterball’s slaughterhouses, 65% of positive samples were resistant to at least one antibiotic drug, compared with 61% at Jennie-O.

Other major suppliers also recorded similar levels of contamination. California-based Foster Farms registered a contamination rate of 29%, with 55% of pathogens resistant. Koch Foods, in Illinois, had a contamination rate of 27%, with 51% resistance.
Neither Foster Farms nor Koch Foods responded to requests for comment.

Steve Roach, program director at Food Animal Concerns Trust and senior analyst for the Keep Antibiotics Working coalition, said: “Antibiotic resistance doesn’t spontaneously generate in wildlife. It’s a result of antibiotic use on farms.” He noted resistance in salmonella is associated with longer disease duration, with “more likelihood of hospitalization, and also more likelihood of death”.

blocks.caption: A truckload of turkeys arrives at the Butterball facility in Mount Olive, North Carolina, on 13 November 2018. Photograph: Michael S Williamson/The Washington Post/Getty Images

blocks.text: Meat companies commonly feed antibiotics to all animals, not just sick ones, government figures show. In 2024, pharmaceutical companies sold 16% more drugs to the animal agriculture industry than in the previous year, according to data from the US Food and Drug Administration.

Replogle of Food & Water Watchsaid: “Pharmaceutical companies wanted to expand their markets, so they started marketing their products as a way to prevent disease.” Antimicrobial resistance is now outpacing the development of new antibiotics in a way that is “very scary” for public health.

The Animal Health Institute, which represents companies making drugs for use in animals, has defended giving healthy animals antibiotics to prevent disease and argued that the meat industry makes a small contribution to antibiotic resistance in humans compared with other sources, such as humans transmitting resistant pathogens to other humans.
The World Health Organization, however, “strongly recommends” against routine use of antibiotics on healthy animals.

The Butterball spokesperson said that 60% of the company’s turkeys did not receive antibiotics last year. “Butterball follows responsible antibiotic use practices that support both animal health and public health,” said Johnson, the Butterball executive.

The Jennie-O spokesperson also commented: “We support responsible antibiotic stewardship through veterinary oversight and the judicious use of antibiotics in accordance with regulatory requirements and animal health best practices.”

Naomi Hallum, co-founder of Project Slingshot, said: “The superbugs are not a contamination problem; they are a factory-farming problem. You cannot keep turkeys alive without antibiotics if you are going to cram them by the thousands inside overcrowded industrial sheds. Antibiotic-resistant disease is an inevitable outcome.”

The Butterball spokesperson also said the company “adheres to science-based animal welfare standards, including requirements for appropriate space allowances that support natural movement, mobility and overall bird health and wellbeing”.

articles.title: Lululemon founder stuns Canadian women’s leadership conference with sexist comments
articles.summary:
Chip Wilson said men importing brides from Thailand was due to women waiting too long to have children

The controversial founder of Lululemon suggested women in

blocks.text: The controversial founder of Lululemon suggested women in Canada are having too few children and this could lead some men to bring in brides from Thailand, in remarks that stunned audience members at a women’s leadership conference.

Chip Wilson, who built the Vancouver yoga-wear startup into a global athleisure empire, was a featured speaker at the Leadership Forum in Calgary earlier this week, an event organized by Axis Connects to advance women in leadership. The organization says it aims to create space for “candid conversations about the barriers women face both in business and society”.

Wilson’s talk on 23 November, titled “Little Black Stretchy Pants” after his memoir, was billed as an “intimate, fireside chat” offering insight into the “mind and instincts of the man himself”. It was moderated by Nuvyn Peters, CEO of Axis Connects.

There is no publicly available video of the event, but the Guardian spoke with people who attended it and reviewed social media posts from those present. Outrage over the event was first reported by the Globe and Mail.

According to people who were there, Wilson told the audience that companies would be reluctant to hire a 22-year-old woman because she might become pregnant at 23 and take maternity leave. He went on to suggest that women were waiting too long to have children, prompting men to import brides from Thailand.
“There were audible gasps in the room and everyone was clearly uncomfortable. It was a mix of disengaging, walking out and also just complete shock of what was being said on stage,” one person said.

“I am floored that Axis gave this man a platform. We all were saying before the event it was surprising he was there – and it’s clear that [Wilson] runs in the organizer’s circles after she opened with the fact that they go on walks [at a Vancouver mountain] together.”
The event, which was supposed to run for an hour, was cut short at 45 minutes.

The remarks are not the first time Wilson has attracted criticism for his comments about women and their bodies. He stepped down as chair of Lululemon’s board in 2013 after the company’s signature black yoga pants were criticized for being see-through and Wilson blamed the problem on the body types of some customers.
On Monday, he reportedly told the group that those prior comments about body types had been “misconstrued” and said he was referring to women who wear sizes that are too small.
Wilson, who is believed to be worth more than C$6bn, has not had a leadership role at Lululemon for several years but remains a major shareholder.
He also reportedly told the audience that poverty had largely been eradicated, and that he was looking forward to going to space with Elon Musk.

Audience members also said Wilson suggested that men were better suited to helm clothing companies that catered to women, because they knew what looked good on women’s bodies. He said the same was true of women who lead companies focused on men’s fashion.

“We recognize that several comments made by Chip Wilson at the Leadership Forum were offensive and inconsistent with the values and mission of Axis Connects,” Peters said in a statement. “We understand why those remarks caused concern and disappointment among members of our community. His comments also underscore an uncomfortable reality: attitudes and assumptions that hold women back in the workplace and in leadership have not disappeared. Challenging those attitudes is central to the work and ethos of Axis Connects.”

Wilson’s spokesperson pointed to the work the Lululemon founder has done to mentor and “empower” women in leadership roles over the years and said his efforts “speak for themselves”. A number of women who were early employees of the company and worked closely with Wilson became millionaires when the company went public, he has previously noted in his memoir, and have gone on to found their own businesses.

More than 700 women attended the conference, many representing organizations they worked for. One person said the experience left her “irate”, adding that it was also indicative of what women continued to tolerate.
“It’s just sad that this is what women still have to deal with, in a forum literally for women.”

articles.title: Top Gear is back in 2028, with chef Gordon Ramsay at the wheel
articles.summary: Rev up those engines — the British show that sparked the now globally-successful Top Gear franchise is returning, with celebrity chef Gordon Ramsay at the wheel as its new main presenter.

image.caption: Celebrity chef Gordon Ramsay is the new presenter of the British motoring show Top Gear, which will be returning with new episodes in 2028, according to the BBC. (BBC Top Gear Magazine)

blocks.text: Entertainment·New
Rev up those engines — the British show that sparked the now globally-successful Top Gear franchise is returning, with celebrity chef Gordon Ramsay at the wheel as its new main presenter.
Show returning 4 years after previous host Andrew 'Freddie' Flintoff's serious crash
Yes, the man who came to fame whipping up high-end food and yelling at hapless would-be-chefs in shows like MasterChef and Hell's Kitchen is now trading in his cooking knives for car keys.

In a video announcing Top Gear's return, Ramsay holds on for dear life in the passenger seat of a sports car as it careens down a track at top speed, the show's eternally-helmeted, iconic stunt driver The Stig in the driver's seat.
"Top Gear is back," Ramsay exclaims over the sound of the engine.

The show has been off the air in the U.K. since previous presenter Andrew 'Freddie' Flintoff suffered serious injuries in a crash on Top Gear's test track during filming in 2023. A safety review was carried out in the months following the crash, but the BBC decided at the time to park the show "for the foreseeable future."
The future, it seems, is here. The show will begin filming next year and will start airing episodes in the U.K. in 2028, according to the BBC.
Ramsay may be better known for his skills in the kitchen, but he has always been a car fan, he said in a BBC Top Gear magazine article announcing his casting.

“My love affair with cars began as a child, growing up a field away from Silverstone, where I would climb over the fences and sneak in for a glimpse of the racing,” Ramsay said. “That early excitement sparked a lifelong passion for cars, motorsport, beautiful design and extraordinary engineering."
In the new series, Ramsay will be joined by a team of as-yet-unrevealed co-presenters and filming will include "locations across the globe," the BBC stated.

items: BBC parks popular Top Gear show after presenter injured

blocks.text: Top Gear is an enduring British show, stretching back to a 1977 show under the BBC. The modern version of the show, which has inspired international formats and spinoffs, started in 2002 and included reviews of cars, vehicular challenges, races and a popular celebrity segment in which celebrity guests competed to set the fastest lap on the Top Gear track.

Ramsay himself has appeared on the show as a guest three times before. The BBC noted that he "once managed to hustle a Chevy Lacetti around the TG Test Track in 1m 46.3s," during the Star in a Reasonably-Priced Car segment, calling him "a dab hand at the track."
The crash that brought Top Gear to a halt wasn't the first time the British show made headlines.

The show fired original co-presenter Jeremy Clarkson — a controversial figure whose bluster helped the show initially find success — in 2015, following a physical altercation with a producer. Clarkson, who had previously been disciplined for allegedly using a racial slur on set, publicly apologized to producer Oisin Tymon in 2016 after Tymon sued for personal injury and racial discrimination.

Following Clarkson's ousting, the show rattled through a roster of co-presenters, including Chris Evans (not that one), Matt LeBlanc and Rory Reid. In 2019, Flintoff took over as main presenter alongside Chris Harris and Paddy McGuinness.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Alexandra Mae Jones is a senior writer for CBC News based in Toronto. She has written on a variety of topics, from health to pop culture to breaking news, and previously reported for CTV News and the Toronto Star. She joined CBC in 2024. You can reach her at alexandra.mae.jones@cbc.ca

articles.title: Israeli judges recommend dropping most serious charges against Netanyahu
articles.summary: The Israeli PM says his trial should end after judges said there was little chance of conviction in one of three cases.

blocks.text: Judges in Israel have suggested prosecutors drop bribery charges against Benjamin Netanyahu, potentially handing the caretaker prime minister a boost as he fights for his political survival.

The judges told the attorney general that there was little chance of conviction in the first of three cases he is facing, in which he is accused of granting government favours in exchange for positive media coverage.
They also questioned whether his actions amounted to criminal conduct in a second corruption case, and suggested prosecutors seek a plea deal in a third.
Netanyahu has consistently denied the allegations against him and called on Wednesday for the trial to be ended "immediately".
"Ten years of terrible suffering for me, my family, my son," he said in a televised statement.
"Ten years of incitement to hatred that wounds the soul."
Netanyahu was first charged in 2019, but court proceedings have been prolonged in part by the recent Israel-Gaza war.

The case now under serious doubt, known as Case 4,000, concerns an alleged "reciprocal arrangement" between Netanyahu and the controlling shareholder in Israel's biggest telecoms company. Both denied any wrongdoing.
In a highly unusual step, a judging panel at the Jerusalem District Court summoned Israeli Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara on Wednesday to express their concerns.
"The chances of conviction are low – to an extent that warrants reconsidering the matter," Judge Rivka Friedman-Feldman told her, Israeli media report.

The judges also cast doubt on whether Netanyahu's actions, which are subject to a second case – concerning another alleged quid-pro-quo with another media baron, known as Case 2,000 – met the threshold for criminality.

While they left open the possibility of a conviction in the third case: Case 1,000, which alleges Netanyahu acted for the benefit of an Australian billionaire after being gifted cigars and champagne by him.
However, the judges told the attorney general that, in the public interest, there needed to be a "rethink" in how the trial should move forward, Israeli media report.
Baharav-Miara said she would consider the judges' recommendations.
It has been six years since Netanyahu became Israel's first sitting prime minister to face a criminal trial.
He has always claimed to be the victim of a political witch-hunt and said on Wednesday that the "fabricated cases" against him were now falling apart.

The cases have continued to progress in court while Netanyahu remained in power throughout the war in Gaza, though judges agreed to reduce the number of hearings due to security concerns around the conflict.
The accusations against him have rocked Israeli politics, fuelling already deep divisions. His trial has coincided with controversial, far-reaching judiciary reforms by Netanyahu's government.
For his opponents, Netanyahu's fear of prison has distorted his decision-making as prime minister and made him especially dependent on his far-right coalition partners to remain in power.

This latest development will give a boost to Netanyahu, whose political opponent Gadi Eisenkot is currently attempting to form a coalition government after an inconclusive general election last month.

While Netanyahu's parliamentary bloc won more seats than that of his rival, both fell short of an outright majority. Israel's president has offered Eisenkot the first chance to form a new administration.
Netanyahu remains subject to an arrest warrant from the International Criminal Court for alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity in Gaza, which he also denies.

articles.title: Health Canada issues warning on rare risk of vision loss with semaglutide GLP-1 drugs
articles.summary: A safety review from Health Canada has found a possible link between semaglutide GLP-1 drugs and a rare form of vision loss.

image.caption: Health Canada has issued a public warning about the 'very rare but serious' risk of vision loss tied to semaglutide GLP-1 drugs. (CBC)

blocks.text: Health·Breaking
A safety review from Health Canada has found a possible link between semaglutide GLP-1 drugs and a rare form of vision loss.
Federal team's safety review found possible link between use of drugs and 'very rare' eye condition
Health Canada has issued a public warning about the "very rare but serious" risk of vision loss tied to semaglutide GLP-1 drugs, known by brand names such as Ozempic, Rybelsus, and Wegovy.

On the heels of similar warnings in the U.S. and Europe, the federal department announced on Wednesday that it had completed its own safety review which found a possible link between prescription semaglutide drugs and the risk of non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION).
Described by Health Canada as "very rare," the eye condition causes sudden, painless blindness or vision changes due to reduced blood flow to the optic nerve.
The condition has no known treatment.
More to come.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Lauren Pelley is a senior health and medical reporter for CBC News. She's a two-time RNAO Media Award winner for in-depth health reporting in 2020 and 2022, a silver medallist for best editorial newsletter at the 2024 Digital Publishing Awards, and a 2024 Covering Climate Now award winner in the health category.
